title.zh: 卷三十三 列傳第二十七: 儒林
title.raw: 卷三十三 列傳第二十七: 儒林 Volume 33: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 蓋今儒者，本因古之六學，斯則王教之典籍，先聖所以明天道，〔一〕正人倫，致治之成法也。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, Confucians today rest on the ancient Six Learnings; these are the canonical books of royal instruction whereby the former sages clarified Heaven's Way, Editorial footnote marker 1. set human relations right, and established the settled methods of bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Confucians today rest on the ancient Six Learnings—the canonical books of royal instruction whereby the former sages clarified Heaven's Way, [1] set human relations right, and established settled methods of bringing order.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇焚書坑儒，六學自此缺矣。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang burned the books and buried the scholars alive; from then on the Six Learnings were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang burned the books and buried the scholars alive; from then on the Six Learnings were lost.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝立五經博士，

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established erudites of the Five Classics,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han established erudites of the Five Classics,

translations.literal: Collation variant: (open).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (open).

sentences.zh: 〔置〕弟子員，〔二〕設科射策，勸以官祿，其傳業者甚眾焉。

translations.literal: set up student quotas, Editorial footnote marker 2. established target-shooting examinations for office, and encouraged them with rank and salary; those who transmitted the learning were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He set up student quotas, [2] established target-shooting examinations for office, and encouraged them with rank and salary; those who transmitted the learning were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 自兩漢登賢，咸資經術。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties onward, those advanced as worthies all relied on classic learning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Two Han dynasties onward, those advanced as worthies all relied on classic learning.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉浮蕩，儒教淪歇，公卿士庶，罕通經業矣。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin, frivolity prevailed and Confucian teaching declined; among grandees, gentry, and commoners, few mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, frivolity prevailed and Confucian teaching declined; among grandees, gentry, and commoners, few mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊之間，國學時復開置。

translations.literal: Between Song and Qi, the National University was from time to time reopened.
translations.idiomatic: Between Song and Qi, the National University was from time to time reopened.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝開五館，建國學，總以五經教授，

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang opened the Five Halls, established the National University, and altogether had the Five Classics taught,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang opened the Five Halls, established the National University, and altogether had the Five Classics taught,

sentences.zh: （唯國學乃經）

translations.literal: Collation variant: (only the National University then the classics).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (only the National University then the classics).

sentences.zh: 經各置助教云。

translations.literal: and for each classic appointed assistant instructors.
translations.idiomatic: For each classic he appointed assistant instructors.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕武帝或紆鑾駕，臨幸庠序，釋奠先師，躬親試冑，申之醼語，勞之束帛，濟濟焉斯蓋一代之盛矣。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. The Emperor would sometimes unbend his imperial carriage and personally visit the schools, perform the libation sacrifice to the former teacher, himself test the students in caps, extend them banquets in discourse, and reward them with bundles of silk—abundant indeed; this was the splendor of an age.
translations.idiomatic: [3] The emperor would sometimes unbend his imperial carriage and personally visit the schools, perform the libation sacrifice to the former teacher, himself test the students in caps, extend them banquets in discourse, and reward them with bundles of silk—abundant indeed; this was the splendor of an age.

sentences.zh: 高祖創業開基，承前代離亂，衣冠殄盡，寇賊未寧，既日不暇給，弗遑勸課。

translations.literal: When the Founder laid the foundations of the state, he inherited the disorders of the previous age; caps and gowns were utterly destroyed and bandits were not yet pacified. With each day too full for his tasks, he had no leisure to encourage instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder laid the foundations of the state, he inherited the disorders of the previous age; caps and gowns were utterly destroyed and bandits were not yet pacified. With each day too full for his tasks, he had no leisure to encourage instruction.

sentences.zh: 世祖以降，稍置學官，雖博延生徒，成業蓋寡。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wen downward, learning officials were gradually set up; though students were broadly recruited, those who completed their studies were few.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen downward, learning officials were gradually set up; though students were broadly recruited, those who completed their studies were few.

sentences.zh: 今之採綴，蓋亦梁之遺儒云。

translations.literal: What is gathered here now are mostly the surviving Confucians of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: What is gathered here now are mostly the surviving Confucians of Liang.

sentences.zh: 沈文阿

translations.literal: Shen Wen'a
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wen'a

sentences.zh: 沈文阿字國衛，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Wen'a, styled Guowei, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wen'a, styled Guowei, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父峻，以儒學聞於梁世，授桂州刺史，不行。

translations.literal: His father Jun was famed in Liang for Confucian learning and was appointed Inspector of Gui, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun was famed in Liang for Confucian learning and was appointed inspector of Gui, but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 文阿性剛彊，有膂力，少習父業，研精章句。

translations.literal: Wen'a was by nature stubborn and strong, with physical strength; in youth he studied his father's profession and probed deeply into chapter-and-verse learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'a was by nature stubborn and strong, with physical strength; in youth he studied his father's profession and probed deeply into chapter-and-verse learning.

sentences.zh: 祖舅太史叔明、舅王慧興並通經術，而文阿頗傳之。

translations.literal: His grandfather's brother-in-law the Grand Astrologer Shuming and his maternal uncle Wang Huixing both mastered classic learning, and Wen'a largely received their transmission.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather's brother-in-law the grand astrologer Shuming and his maternal uncle Wang Huixing both mastered classic learning, and Wen'a largely received their transmission.

sentences.zh: 又博採先儒異同，自為義疏。

translations.literal: He also broadly collected the agreements and differences of earlier Confucians and composed expository commentaries of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He also broadly collected the agreements and differences of earlier Confucians and composed expository commentaries of his own.

sentences.zh: 治三禮、三傳。

translations.literal: He mastered the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，為梁臨川王國侍郎，累遷兼國子助教、五經博士。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he became an aide in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Linchuan, and was repeatedly promoted to concurrent National University assistant instructor and erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he became an aide in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Linchuan, and was repeatedly promoted to concurrent national university assistant instructor and erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，引為學士，深相禮遇，及撰長春義記，多使文阿撮異聞以廣之。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace, he was brought in as an academician and received deep courtesy; when the emperor compiled the Record of the Everlasting Spring, he often had Wen'a gather divergent accounts to enlarge it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace, he was brought in as an academician and received deep courtesy; when the emperor compiled the Record of the Everlasting Spring, he often had Wen'a gather divergent accounts to enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇逆，簡文別遣文阿招募士卒，入援京師。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jianwen separately sent Wen'a to recruit soldiers to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jianwen separately sent Wen'a to recruit soldiers to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 城陷，與張嵊共保吳興，嵊敗，文阿竄于山野。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he and Zhang Song together held Wuxing; when Song was defeated, Wen'a fled into the mountains and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he and Zhang Song together held Wuxing; when Song was defeated, Wen'a fled into the mountains and wilds.

sentences.zh: 景素聞其名，求之甚急，文阿窮迫不知所出，登樹自縊，遇有所親救之，便自投而下，折其左臂。

translations.literal: Jing had long heard his name and sought him urgently; Wen'a, hard pressed and not knowing where to turn, climbed a tree to hang himself, but a kinsman happened to save him; he then threw himself down and broke his left arm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had long heard his name and sought him urgently; Wen'a, hard pressed and not knowing where to turn, climbed a tree to hang himself, but a kinsman happened to save him; he then threw himself down and broke his left arm.

sentences.zh: 及景平，高祖以文阿州里，表為原鄉令，監江陰郡。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, the Founder, because Wen'a was from his home district, memorialized to make him magistrate of Yuanxiang and overseer of Jiangyin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, the Founder, because Wen'a was from his home district, memorialized to make him magistrate of Yuanxiang and overseer of Jiangyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，入為國子博士，尋領步兵校尉，兼掌儀禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he entered service as erudite of the National University, and soon held concurrently the post of footsoldiers commandant and charge of ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 1 (555) he entered service as erudite of the national university, and soon held concurrently the post of footsoldiers commandant and charge of ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 自太清之亂，臺閣故事，無有存者，文阿父峻，梁武世嘗掌朝儀，頗有遺藁，於是斟酌裁撰，禮度皆自之出。

translations.literal: From the Taqing turmoil onward, the precedents of the palace offices had nothing left preserved; Wen'a's father Jun in Emperor Wu of Liang's time had once held charge of court ceremony and had left considerable drafts, and so Wen'a weighed and trimmed them to compose anew—ceremonial norms all issued from him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taqing turmoil onward, the precedents of the palace offices had nothing left preserved; Wen'a's father Jun in Emperor Wu of Liang's time had once held charge of court ceremony and had left considerable drafts, and so Wen'a weighed and trimmed them to compose anew—ceremonial norms all issued from him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，文阿輒棄官還武康，高祖大怒，發使往誅之。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Wen'a at once left office and returned to Wukang; the Founder was greatly angered and sent envoys to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, Wen'a at once left office and returned to Wukang; the Founder was greatly angered and sent envoys to execute him.

sentences.zh: 時文阿宗人沈恪為郡，請使者寬其死，即面縛鎖頸致於高祖，高祖視而笑曰：「腐儒復何為者？

translations.literal: At that time Wen'a's clansman Shen Ke was administrator of the commandery; he asked the envoys to spare his life, then bound him with his face exposed and the collar locked and delivered him to the Founder. The Founder looked at him and laughed, saying, "What is a rotten Confucian good for?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wen'a's clansman Shen Ke was administrator of the commandery; he asked the envoys to spare his life, then bound him with his face exposed and the collar locked and delivered him to the Founder. The Founder looked at him and laughed, saying, "What is a rotten Confucian good for?

sentences.zh: 」遂赦之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，文阿與尚書左丞徐陵、中書舍人劉師知等議大行皇帝靈座俠御衣服之制，語在師知傳。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, Wen'a together with Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Ling, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, and others debated the regulations for the garments of the attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat and imperial couch on the great journey; the discussion is in Shizhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died, Wen'a together with left vice director Xu Ling, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, and others debated the regulations for the garments of the attendants at the late emperor's spirit seat and imperial couch on the great journey; the discussion is in Shizhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 及世祖即皇帝位，剋日謁廟，尚書右丞庾持奉詔遣博士議其禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the imperial throne, on the appointed day he visited the ancestral temple; Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Chi, Editorial footnote marker 4. received the edict and sent erudites to debate the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen assumed the imperial throne, on the appointed day he visited the ancestral temple; right vice director Yu Chi, [4] received the edict and sent erudites to debate the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕文阿議曰：

translations.literal: Wen'a argued:
translations.idiomatic: Wen'a argued:

sentences.zh: 民物推移，質文殊軌，聖賢因機而立教，王公隨時以適宜。

translations.literal: Things among the people shift; substance and ornament differ in their tracks; sages establish teaching according to the occasion, and kings and dukes adapt to what is fitting for the time.
translations.idiomatic: Things among the people shift; substance and ornament differ in their tracks; sages establish teaching according to the occasion, and kings and dukes adapt to what is fitting for the time.

sentences.zh: 夫千人無君，不散則亂，萬乘無主，不危則亡。

translations.literal: When a thousand men have no lord, if they do not disperse they fall into disorder; when the myriad chariots have no master, if there is no peril they perish.
translations.idiomatic: When a thousand men have no lord, if they do not disperse they fall into disorder; when the myriad chariots have no master, if there is no peril they perish.

sentences.zh: 當隆周之日，公旦叔父，呂、召爪牙，成王在喪，禍幾覆國。

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of high Zhou, the Duke of Zhou was uncle and minister, Lü and Shao were talons and teeth; King Cheng was in mourning and disaster nearly overturned the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the flourishing age of high Zhou, the Duke of Zhou was uncle and minister, Lü and Shao were talons and teeth; King Cheng was in mourning and disaster nearly overturned the state.

sentences.zh: 是以既葬便有公冠之儀，始殯受麻冕之策。

translations.literal: Therefore, once the burial was completed there was at once the ceremony of the ducal cap; at the first encoffining he received the policy of the hemp cap and mourning robe.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, once the burial was completed there was at once the ceremony of the ducal cap; at the first encoffining he received the policy of the hemp cap and mourning robe.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋示天下以有主，慮社稷之艱難。

translations.literal: This was to show the realm that there was a lord and to take thought for the hardship of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: This was to show the realm that there was a lord and to take thought for the hardship of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 逮乎末葉縱橫，漢承其弊，雖文、景刑厝，而七國連兵。

translations.literal: Down to the late age of contending states, Han inherited its abuses; though Wen and Jing suspended punishments, the Seven States still linked arms in war.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the late age of contending states, Han inherited its abuses; though Wen and Jing suspended punishments, the Seven States still linked arms in war.

sentences.zh: 或踰月即尊，或崩日稱詔，此皆有為而為之，非無心於禮制也。

translations.literal: Some took the throne after a month, some proclaimed edicts on the day of the death—these were all done with purpose and were not without concern for ritual institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Some took the throne after a month, some proclaimed edicts on the day of the death—these were all done with purpose and were not without concern for ritual institutions.

sentences.zh: 今國諱之日，雖抑哀於璽紱之重，猶未序於君臣之儀。

translations.literal: Now on the day of the state's mourning taboo, though grief is restrained by the weight of the seal and sash, the order between ruler and minister has not yet been set.
translations.idiomatic: Now on the day of the state's mourning taboo, though grief is restrained by the weight of the seal and sash, the order between ruler and minister has not yet been set.

sentences.zh: 古禮，朝廟退坐正寢，聽群臣之政，今皇帝拜廟還，宜御太極殿，以正南面之尊，此即周康在朝一二臣衛者也。

translations.literal: In ancient rites, after retiring from the temple audience one sat in the main chamber and heard the ministers' government; now when the emperor returns from bowing at the temple, he should take his seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to set right the dignity of facing south—this is like King Kang of Zhou in court with one or two ministers guarding him.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient rites, after retiring from the temple audience one sat in the main chamber and heard the ministers' government; now when the emperor returns from bowing at the temple, he should take his seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to set right the dignity of facing south—this is like King Kang of Zhou in court with one or two ministers guarding him.

sentences.zh: 其壤奠之節，周禮以玉作贄，公侯以珪，子男執璧，此瑞玉也。

translations.literal: As for the rite of laying the offering in the burial mound, the Rites of Zhou take jade to make the tribute-gift: dukes and marquises use the gui, viscounts and barons hold the bi—this is auspicious jade.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rite of laying the offering in the burial mound, the Rites of Zhou take jade to make the tribute-gift: dukes and marquises use the gui, viscounts and barons hold the bi—this is auspicious jade.

sentences.zh: 奠贄既竟，又復致享，天子以璧，王后用琮。

translations.literal: Once the tribute-gift offering was finished, they again presented the offering of enjoyment; the Son of Heaven used the bi, the queen used the cong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the tribute-gift offering was finished, they again presented the offering of enjoyment; the Son of Heaven used the bi, the queen used the cong.

sentences.zh: 秦燒經典，威儀散滅，叔孫通定禮，尤失前憲，奠贄不珪，致享無帛，公王同璧，鴻臚奏賀。

translations.literal: Qin burned the classics; regalia and ceremony scattered and perished; when Shusun Tong fixed the rites, he especially lost the former statutes—the tribute-gift offering had no gui, the enjoyment offering had no silk, dukes and kings alike used the bi, and the Court Chamberlain presented congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Qin burned the classics; regalia and ceremony scattered and perished; when Shusun Tong fixed the rites, he especially lost the former statutes—the tribute-gift offering had no gui, the enjoyment offering had no silk, dukes and kings alike used the bi, and the court chamberlain presented congratulations.

sentences.zh: 若此數事，未聞於古，後相沿襲，至梁行之。

translations.literal: Matters such as these are not heard of in antiquity; later ages handed them down in succession, down to Liang, which practiced them.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as these are not heard of in antiquity; later ages handed them down in succession, down to Liang, which practiced them.

sentences.zh: 夫稱觴奉壽，家國大慶，四廂雅樂，歌奏懽欣。

translations.literal: Raising the cup and offering longevity is the great celebration of state and family; in the four side halls elegant music is played and songs of joy are performed.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the cup and offering longevity is the great celebration of state and family; in the four side halls elegant music is played and songs of joy are performed.

sentences.zh: 今君臣吞哀，萬民抑割，豈同於惟新之禮乎？

translations.literal: Now ruler and ministers swallow grief and the myriad people restrain their sorrow—how can this be the same as the rites of renewal?
translations.idiomatic: Now ruler and ministers swallow grief and the myriad people restrain their sorrow—how can this be the same as the rites of renewal?

sentences.zh: 且周康賓稱奉珪，無萬壽之獻，此則前準明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in King Kang's guest-rite they offered the gui in homage but there was no presentation of ten thousand years of life—here the earlier standard is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in King Kang's guest-rite they offered the gui in homage but there was no presentation of ten thousand years of life—here the earlier standard is clear.

sentences.zh: 三宿三吒，上宗曰饗，斯蓋祭儐受福，寧謂賀酒邪！

translations.literal: Three nights of lodging and three calls of warning—the upper sacrifice is called the offering; this is surely the ritual of the feast-guest receiving blessing—how can it be called congratulatory wine!
translations.idiomatic: Three nights of lodging and three calls of warning—the upper sacrifice is called the offering; this is surely the ritual of the feast-guest receiving blessing—how can it be called congratulatory wine!

sentences.zh: 愚以今坐正殿，止行薦璧之儀，無賀酒之禮。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that on this occasion, sitting in the main hall, one should perform only the rite of presenting the bi on the mat and have no congratulatory wine.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hold that on this occasion, sitting in the main hall, one should perform only the rite of presenting the bi on the mat and have no congratulatory wine.

sentences.zh: 謹撰謁廟還升正寢、群臣陪薦儀注如別。

translations.literal: I respectfully draft the protocol for returning from the temple audience, ascending the main chamber, and the ministers attending with the offering, as set forth separately.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully draft the protocol for returning from the temple audience, ascending the main chamber, and the ministers attending with the offering, as set forth separately.

sentences.zh: 詔可施行。

translations.literal: An edict approved and ordered it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved and ordered it implemented.

sentences.zh: 尋遷通直散騎常侍，兼國子博士，領羽林監，仍令於東宮講孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry, concurrent erudite of the National University, and charge of the Feathered Forest guard; he was still ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry, concurrent erudite of the national university, and charge of the feathered forest guard; he was still ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 4 (563) he died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔贈廷尉卿。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 文阿所撰儀禮八十餘卷，經典大義十八卷，並行於世，諸儒多傳其學。

translations.literal: Wen'a's compositions on ceremonial regulations, more than eighty juan, and Great Meanings of the Classics, eighteen juan, all circulated in the world; many Confucians transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'a's compositions on ceremonial regulations, more than eighty juan, and Great Meanings of the Classics, eighteen juan, all circulated in the world; many Confucians transmitted his learning.

sentences.zh: 沈洙字弘道，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Zhu, styled Hongdao, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhu, styled Hongdao, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖休稚，〔五〕梁餘杭令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuzhi, Editorial footnote marker 5. was Liang magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuzhi, [5] was Liang magistrate of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 父山卿，梁國子博士、中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Shanqing was a Liang erudite of the National University and gentleman of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanqing was a Liang erudite of the national university and gentleman of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 洙少方雅好學，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Zhu from youth was proper and elegant, fond of learning, and did not make friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu from youth was proper and elegant, fond of learning, and did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 治三禮、春秋左氏傳。

translations.literal: He mastered the Three Rites and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 精識彊記，五經章句，諸子史書，問無不答。

translations.literal: With keen understanding and strong memory, on the chapter-and-verse of the Five Classics and the books of the masters and histories, there was nothing he could not answer when asked.
translations.idiomatic: With keen understanding and strong memory, on the chapter-and-verse of the Five Classics and the books of the masters and histories, there was nothing he could not answer when asked.

sentences.zh: 解巾梁湘東王國左常侍，轉中軍宣城王限內參軍，板仁威臨賀王記室參軍，遷尚書祠部郎中，時年蓋二十餘。

translations.literal: He doffed the headcloth as left regular attendant of Liang's Prince of Xiangdong's establishment, was moved to inner aide in the central army of the Prince of Xuancheng, was appointed recorder in the establishment of the Prince of Linhe of Renwei, and was promoted to director of the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Sacrifices—he was then a little over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: He doffed the headcloth as left regular attendant of Liang's Prince of Xiangdong's establishment, was moved to inner aide in the central army of the Prince of Xuancheng, was appointed recorder in the establishment of the Prince of Linhe of Renwei, and was promoted to director of the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Sacrifices—he was then a little over twenty.

sentences.zh: 大同中，學者多涉獵文史，不為章句，而洙獨積思經術，吳郡朱异、會稽賀琛甚嘉之。

translations.literal: In the Datong period, many students ranged widely through literature and history and did not work on chapter-and-verse, but Zhu alone piled thought on classic learning; Zhu Yi of Wu commandery and He Chen of Kuaiji greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong period, many students ranged widely through literature and history and did not work on chapter-and-verse, but Zhu alone piled thought on classic learning; Zhu Yi of Wu commandery and He Chen of Kuaiji greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 及异、琛於士林館講制旨義，常使洙為都講。

translations.literal: When Yi and Chen lectured on the imperially directed meanings at the Forest of Scholars Hall, Zhu was regularly made chief expounder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and Chen lectured on the imperially directed meanings at the Forest of Scholars Hall, Zhu was regularly made chief expounder.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，洙竄於臨安，時世祖在焉，親就習業。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhu fled to Lin'an; at that time Emperor Wen was there and personally came to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhu fled to Lin'an; at that time Emperor Wen was there and personally came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入輔，除國子博士，與沈文阿同掌儀禮。

translations.literal: When the Founder entered as regent, Zhu was made erudite of the National University and together with Shen Wen'a held charge of ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder entered as regent, Zhu was made erudite of the national university and together with Shen Wen'a held charge of ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加員外散騎常侍，歷揚州別駕從事史、大匠卿。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Zhu was additionally made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and served in succession as aide in the Yangzhou separate office, grand director of works,
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, Zhu was additionally made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and served in succession as aide in the Yangzhou separate office, grand director of works,

sentences.zh: 有司奏前寧遠將軍、建康令沈孝軌門生陳三兒牒稱主人翁靈柩在周，主人奉使關內，因欲迎喪，久而未返。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized that the former General Who Pacifies the Distance and magistrate of Jiankang Shen Xiaogui's student Chen San'er submitted a petition stating that his master's father's coffin was in Zhou, that the master was on mission within the passes and wished to bring back the coffin, but had long failed to return.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialized that the former general who pacifies the distance and magistrate of Jiankang Shen Xiaogui's student Chen San'er submitted a petition stating that his master's father's coffin was in Zhou, that the master was on mission within the passes and wished to bring back the coffin, but had long failed to return.

sentences.zh: 此月晦即是再周，主人弟息見在此者，為至月末除靈，內外即吉？

translations.literal: The end of this month is the second anniversary; the master's younger brother and son who are here—should they remove the spirit by month's end and the inner and outer circles observe auspicious dress?
translations.idiomatic: The end of this month is the second anniversary; the master's younger brother and son who are here—should they remove the spirit by month's end and the inner and outer circles observe auspicious dress?

sentences.zh: 為待主人還情禮申竟？

translations.literal: Or should they wait until the master returns and the propriety of feeling is fully carried through?
translations.idiomatic: Or should they wait until the master returns and the propriety of feeling is fully carried through?

sentences.zh: 以事諮左丞江德藻，德藻議：「王衛軍云：『久喪不葬，唯主人不變，其餘親各終月數而除。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Left Vice Director Jiang Dezao; Dezao argued: "Wang Weijun said: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the master does not change; the rest of the kin each complete the month-count and remove mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to left vice director Jiang Dezao; Dezao argued: "Wang Weijun said: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the master does not change; the rest of the kin each complete the month-count and remove mourning.'

sentences.zh: 』此蓋引禮文論在家內有事故未得葬者耳。

translations.literal: This is citing ritual text to discuss those at home who have an affair and have not yet been able to bury.
translations.idiomatic: This is citing ritual text to discuss those at home who have an affair and have not yet been able to bury.

sentences.zh: 孝軌既在異域，雖已迎喪，還期無指，諸弟若遂不除，永絕婚嫁，此於人情，或為未允。

translations.literal: Xiaogui is in a foreign land; though he has already sent to bring back the coffin, the date of return is uncertain; if the younger brothers proceed at once to remove mourning, they would forever cut off marriage—this in human feeling may perhaps not be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogui is in a foreign land; though he has already sent to bring back the coffin, the date of return is uncertain; if the younger brothers proceed at once to remove mourning, they would forever cut off marriage—this in human feeling may perhaps not be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 中原淪陷已後，理有事例，宜諮沈常侍詳議。

translations.literal: After the Central Plains fell, there have been cases in principle; the regular attendant Shen should be consulted for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains fell, there have been cases in principle; the regular attendant Shen should be consulted for detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 」洙議曰：「禮有變正，又有從宜。

translations.literal: Zhu argued:
translations.idiomatic: Zhu argued:

sentences.zh: 禮小記云：『久而不葬者，唯主

translations.literal: Rites have the orthodox and also adaptation to what is fitting. The Record of Smaller Matters in Rites says: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the chief
translations.idiomatic: Rites have the orthodox and also adaptation to what is fitting. The Record of Smaller Matters in Rites says: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the chief

translations.literal: Collation variant: (sacrifice).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (sacrifice).

sentences.zh: 〔喪〕者不除，〔六〕其餘以麻終月數者除喪則已。

translations.literal: mourner does not remove mourning; Editorial footnote marker 6. the rest, when the hemp month-count is completed, remove mourning and that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: The mourner does not remove mourning; [6] the rest, when the hemp month-count is completed, remove mourning and that is all.'

sentences.zh: 』注云：『其餘謂傍親。

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'The rest means collateral kin.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: 'The rest means collateral kin.'

sentences.zh: 』如鄭所解，眾子皆應不除，王衛軍所引，此蓋禮之正也。

translations.literal: As Zheng interprets it, all the sons should not remove mourning; what Wang Weijun cited is the orthodox of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng interprets it, all the sons should not remove mourning; what Wang Weijun cited is the orthodox of the rites.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕但魏氏東關之役，既失亡屍柩，葬禮無期，議以為禮無終身之喪，故制使除服。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 7. But in Wei, at the eastern-pass campaign, when the corpse and coffin were lost and burial had no set date, deliberation held that the rites have no mourning for a lifetime, and so regulations were made to remove the garments.
translations.idiomatic: [7] But in Wei, at the eastern-pass campaign, when the corpse and coffin were lost and burial had no set date, deliberation held that the rites have no mourning for a lifetime, and so regulations were made to remove the garments.

sentences.zh: 晉氏喪亂，或死於虜庭，無由迎殯，江左故復申明其制。

translations.literal: In Jin, amid mourning turmoil, some died in the barbarian court with no means to bring the coffin home; south of the Yangtze they therefore again clarified the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, amid mourning turmoil, some died in the barbarian court with no means to bring the coffin home; south of the Yangtze they therefore again clarified the regulation.

sentences.zh: 李胤之祖，王華之父，並存亡不測，其子制服依時釋縗，此並變禮之宜也。

translations.literal: Li Yin's grandfather and Wang Hua's father were both alive or dead unknown; their sons put on mourning garments and released the hemp at the proper time—these are all cases of adapting the rites to what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin's grandfather and Wang Hua's father were both alive or dead unknown; their sons put on mourning garments and released the hemp at the proper time—these are all cases of adapting the rites to what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 孝軌雖因奉使便欲迎喪，而戎狄難親，還期未剋。

translations.literal: Though Xiaogui, because he was on mission, wished to bring back the coffin, the barbarians are hard to approach and the date of return is not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaogui, because he was on mission, wished to bring back the coffin, the barbarians are hard to approach and the date of return is not yet fixed.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜依東關故事，在此國內者，並應釋除縗麻，毀靈附祭，若喪柩得還，別行改葬之禮。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that one should follow the eastern-pass precedent: those within this state should all release the hemp garments, destroy the spirit seat, and attach the sacrifice; if the coffin can be brought back, a separate ceremony of reburial should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hold that one should follow the eastern-pass precedent: those within this state should all release the hemp garments, destroy the spirit seat, and attach the sacrifice; if the coffin can be brought back, a separate ceremony of reburial should be performed.

sentences.zh: 自天下寇亂，西朝傾覆，流播絕域，情禮莫申，若此之徒，諒非一二，寧可喪期無數，而弗除衰服，朝庭自應為之限制，以義斷恩，通訪博識，折之禮衷。

translations.literal: Since the realm fell into bandit turmoil and the western court was overturned, people were cast to remote regions and feeling and propriety could not be expressed—such persons surely are not one or two; how can mourning periods be without number while they do not remove the mourning garments? The court itself should set limits, cutting affection by right, and broadly consult the learned to settle it at the center of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Since the realm fell into bandit turmoil and the western court was overturned, people were cast to remote regions and feeling and propriety could not be expressed—such persons surely are not one or two; how can mourning periods be without number while they do not remove the mourning garments? The court itself should set limits, cutting affection by right, and broadly consult the learned to settle it at the center of the rites.

sentences.zh: 」德藻依洙議，奏可。

translations.literal: Dezao followed Zhu's argument; the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao followed Zhu's argument; the memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遷通直散騎常侍，侍東宮讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the throne, Zhu was moved to regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry and lectured in attendance in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen assumed the throne, Zhu was moved to regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry and lectured in attendance in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書左丞，領揚州大中正，遷光祿卿，侍讀如故。

translations.literal: Soon he held concurrently the post of Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and charge of the Yangzhou chief rectifier, was moved to Minister of the Household, and his lecturing attendance remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held concurrently the post of left vice director of the Masters of Writing and charge of the Yangzhou chief rectifier, was moved to minister of the household, and his lecturing attendance remained as before.

sentences.zh: 廢帝嗣位，重為通直散騎常侍，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhu again became regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry and concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhu again became regular attendant of the direct and unbent scattered cavalry and concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遷戎昭將軍、輕車衡陽王長史，行府國事，帶琅邪、彭城二郡丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Displays Martial Might and chief clerk to the Prince of Hengyang of the Light Chariots, acting in the prince's establishment affairs, with concurrent charge as commandery aide of Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to general who displays martial might and chief clerk to the Prince of Hengyang of the Light Chariots, acting in the prince's establishment affairs, with concurrent charge as commandery aide of Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 梁代舊律，測囚之法，日一上，起自晡鼓，盡于二更。

translations.literal: Under Liang's old statutes, the method of pressing prisoners for confession was once a day, beginning at the twilight drum and ending at the second watch.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang's old statutes, the method of pressing prisoners for confession was once a day, beginning at the twilight drum and ending at the second watch.

sentences.zh: 及比部郎范泉刪定律令，以舊法測立時久，非人所堪，分其刻數，日再上。

translations.literal: When Director of the Bureau of Review Fan Quan revised the statutes and ordinances, because the old method of pressing by time was long and not what a man could bear, he divided the time-markers and made it twice a day.
translations.idiomatic: When director of the Bureau of Review Fan Quan revised the statutes and ordinances, because the old method of pressing by time was long and not what a man could bear, he divided the time-markers and made it twice a day.

sentences.zh: 廷尉以為新制過輕，請集八座丞郎并祭酒孔奐、行事沈洙五舍人會尚書省詳議。

translations.literal: The Court Tribunal held that the new regulation was too light and requested that the eight chief ministers, directors and vice directors, together with libationer Kong Huan and acting officer Shen Zhu and the five attendants meet in the Masters of Writing office for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The court tribunal held that the new regulation was too light and requested that the eight chief ministers, directors and vice directors, together with libationer Kong Huan and acting officer Shen Zhu and the five attendants meet in the Masters of Writing office for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時高宗錄尚書，集眾議之，都官尚書周弘正曰：「未知獄所測人，有幾人款？

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he gathered the assembly to debate it. Director of Punishments Zhou Hongzheng said: "It is not known how many persons in the prison are pressed for confession—how many confess?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuan was recorder of the Masters of Writing; he gathered the assembly to debate it. Director of Punishments Zhou Hongzheng said, "It is not known how many persons in the prison are pressed for confession—how many confess?

sentences.zh: 幾人不款？

translations.literal: How many did not confess?
translations.idiomatic: How many did not confess?

sentences.zh: 須前責取人名及數并其罪目，然後更集。

translations.literal: First the names and numbers must be obtained along with their charges, and then we shall convene again.
translations.idiomatic: First obtain the prisoners' names, their number, and the charges against them, then convene again.

sentences.zh: 」得廷尉監沈仲由列稱，別制已後，有壽羽兒一人坐殺壽慧，劉磊渴等八人坐偷馬仗家口渡北，依法測之，限訖不款。

translations.literal: " The Court Tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou then submitted a list, saying that since the new regulations there had been one Shou Yu'er convicted of killing Shou Hui, and eight men including Liu Leike convicted of stealing horses and taking household members north across the border; interrogated under the law to the time limit, none confessed.
translations.idiomatic: " Court tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou then listed cases since the new rules: one Shou Yu'er for killing Shou Hui, and Liu Leike and seven others for stealing horses and taking dependents north; all were interrogated under law to the time limit without confessing.

sentences.zh: 劉道朔坐犯七改偷，依法測立，首尾二日而款。

translations.literal: Liu Daoshuo was convicted of seven counts of theft; interrogated under the law, he confessed within two days from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoshuo was convicted of seven thefts; under legal interrogation he confessed within two days.

sentences.zh: 陳法滿坐被使封藏、阿法受錢，未及上而款。

translations.literal: Chen Manman was convicted of being sent to seal stores and Afu accepting money; before the session was up he confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Manman was convicted of sealing stores on commission and Afu taking bribes; he confessed before the session ended.

sentences.zh: 弘正議曰：「凡小大之獄，必應以情，正言依準五聽，驗其虛實，豈可全恣考掠，以判刑罪。

translations.literal: Hongzheng argued: "In great and small cases alike one must proceed by the facts, speak straight and follow the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can one wholly rely on beating under examination to fix guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng argued, "Cases great and small must follow the facts, apply the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can guilt be fixed wholly by torture in examination?

sentences.zh: 且測人時節，本非古制，近代已來，方有此法。

translations.literal: Moreover the seasons for interrogation under torture are not an ancient institution; only in recent times has this method appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the hours for interrogation under torture are not ancient; only in recent times has this method existed.

sentences.zh: 起自晡鼓，迄于二更，豈是常人所能堪忍？

translations.literal: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—can ordinary men endure it?
translations.idiomatic: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—is that something ordinary men can endure?

sentences.zh: 所以重械之下，危墯之上，無人不服，誣枉者多。

translations.literal: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and many are wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and wrongful convictions are many.

sentences.zh: 朝晚二時，同等刻數，進退而求，於事為衷。

translations.literal: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra counts, weighed forward and back, hit the mean for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra counts, weighed together, strike the right balance.

sentences.zh: 若謂小促前期，致實罪不伏，如復時節延長，則無愆妄款。

translations.literal: If one says shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to submit, then extending the season would leave no false confessions.
translations.idiomatic: If shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to confess, extending the hours would leave no false confessions.

sentences.zh: 且人之所堪，既有彊弱，人之立意，固亦多途。

translations.literal: Moreover what men can bear differs in strength, and how men set their minds also follows many paths.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover endurance differs by strength, and men's resolve follows many paths.

sentences.zh: 至如貫高榜笞刺爇，身無完者，〔八〕戴就熏針並極，困篤不移，豈關時刻長短，掠測優劣？

translations.literal: Take for example Guan Gao, flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole, [8] or Dai Jiu, smoked with needles to the utmost yet unshaken in distress—what has that to do with the length of the hours or whether interrogation is harsh or mild?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao was flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole [8]; Dai Jiu was smoked with needles to the utmost yet would not yield—what has that to do with the length of the hours or the severity of interrogation?

sentences.zh: 夫與殺不辜，寧失不經，罪疑惟輕，功疑惟重，斯則古之聖王，垂此明法。

translations.literal: Rather than kill the innocent, better to miss punishing the guilty; when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy: such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than kill the innocent, better to let the guilty go unpunished; when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy—such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.

sentences.zh: 愚謂依范泉著制，於事為允。

translations.literal: I hold that following Fan Quan's established regulations is acceptable for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that following Fan Quan's regulations is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」舍人盛權議曰：「比部范泉新制，尚書周弘正明議，咸允虞書惟輕之旨，殷頌敷正之言。

translations.literal: " Attendant Sheng Quan argued: "The new regulations of the Ministry of Justice Fan Quan and the clear argument of Minister Zhou Hongzheng both accord with the intent of the Yu canon to lean light and the Yin hymn to spread rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant Sheng Quan argued, "Fan Quan's new regulations at the ministry of justice and Minister Zhou Hongzheng's clear argument both accord with the Yu canon to lean light and the Yin hymn to spread rectitude.

sentences.zh: 竊尋廷尉監沈仲由等列新制以後，凡有獄十一人，其所測者十人，款者唯一。

translations.literal: I have examined the list of Court Tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou and others: since the new regulations there have been eleven cases in all; ten were interrogated, and only one confessed.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined Shen Zhongyou's list: since the new rules there have been eleven cases; ten were interrogated, and only one confessed.

sentences.zh: 愚謂染罪之囚，獄官宜明加辯析，窮考事理。

translations.literal: I hold that for prisoners tainted with guilt, prison officials should clearly argue and analyze and exhaust the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that for prisoners tainted with guilt, officials should argue the case clearly and exhaust the facts.

sentences.zh: 若罪有可疑，自宜啟審分判，幸無濫測；

translations.literal: If the crime is doubtful, they should themselves open review and divide judgment, and by good fortune not interrogate at random;
translations.idiomatic: If the crime is doubtful, they should open review and divide judgment, and not interrogate at random;

sentences.zh: 若罪有實驗，乃可啟審測立；

translations.literal: if the crime is clearly proved, only then may they open review and set interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: if the crime is clearly proved, only then may they set interrogation;

sentences.zh: 此則枉直有分，刑宥斯理。

translations.literal: then crooked and straight have their division, and mercy in punishment follows reason.
translations.idiomatic: then guilt and innocence are distinguished, and mercy in punishment follows reason.

sentences.zh: 范泉今牒述漢律，云『死罪及除名，罪證明白，考掠已至，而抵隱不服者，處當列上』。

translations.literal: Fan Quan now in his memorial cites Han law, saying: 'For capital crimes and removal from the registers, when the proof of guilt is clear and beating under examination has already been applied yet the accused still conceals and will not submit, the case should be listed and sent up.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Quan's memorial cites Han law: "For capital crimes and removal from the registers, when proof is clear and beating under examination has been applied yet the accused still conceals and will not submit, the case should be listed and sent up."

sentences.zh: 杜預注云『處當，證驗明白之狀，列其抵隱之意』。

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary says: 'Listed up means the clearly proved circumstances, listing the intent to conceal.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's commentary says, "Listed up means the clearly proved circumstances, listing the intent to conceal."

sentences.zh: 竊尋舊制深峻，百中不款者一，新制寬優，十中不款者九，參會兩文，寬猛寔異，處當列上，未見釐革。

translations.literal: I find the old regulations severe: of a hundred, one did not confess; the new regulations are lenient: of ten, nine did not confess. Comparing the two texts, leniency and severity truly differ, yet 'listed and sent up' is nowhere revised.
translations.idiomatic: The old rules were severe: one in a hundred did not confess; the new rules are lenient: nine in ten did not confess. The two texts differ in leniency and severity, yet "listed and sent up" is nowhere revised.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜付典法，更詳『處當列上』之文。

translations.literal: I hold that the matter should be referred to the codex office to examine further the text 'listed and sent up.'
translations.idiomatic: I hold the matter should go to the codex office to examine further the phrase "listed and sent up."

sentences.zh: 洙以太建元年卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Zhu died in the first year of Taijian, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu died in year 1 of Taijian, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 戚羇字公文，吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Qi Ji, styled Gongwen, was a native of Yanguan in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Ji, styled Gongwen, was from Yanguan in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖顯，齊給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian was Qi Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian was Qi supervisor of attendants.

sentences.zh: 父霸，梁臨賀王府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Ba was Liang Central Army Major in the Prince of Linhe's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ba was Liang central army major in the Prince of Linhe's household.

sentences.zh: 羇少聰慧，遊學京都，受三禮於國子助教劉文紹，一二年中，大義略備。

translations.literal: Ji from youth was clever; he traveled to study in the capital and received the Three Rites from Erudite Assistant Liu Wenshao; within a year or two he had the great principles largely in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was clever from youth; he studied in the capital under erudite assistant Liu Wenshao in the Three Rites and within a year or two had the great principles largely in hand.

sentences.zh: 年十九，梁武帝敕策孔子正言并周禮、禮記義，羇對高第。

translations.literal: At nineteen, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered an examination on the Correct Meaning of Confucius and the meanings of the Zhou li and Li ji; Ji placed at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, Emperor Wu of Liang examined him on the Correct Meaning of Confucius and the Zhou li and Li ji; Ji placed at the top.

sentences.zh: 仍除揚州祭酒從事史。

translations.literal: He was then made Retainer of the Libationer of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made retainer of the libationer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 就國子博士宋懷方質儀禮義，懷方北人，自魏攜儀禮、禮記疏，祕惜不傳，及將亡，謂家人曰「吾死後，戚生若赴，便以儀禮、禮記義本付之，若其不來，即宜隨屍而殯」。

translations.literal: He went to Erudite Song Huaifang of the Imperial Academy to question the meaning of the Yi li; Huaifang was a northerner who had brought from Wei commentaries on the Yi li and Li ji, kept secret and not transmitted. When he was about to die he told his family: "After my death, if Student Qi comes, give him the texts of the Yi li and Li ji meanings; if he does not come, bury them with my corpse."
translations.idiomatic: He went to imperial academy erudite Song Huaifang to question the Yi li; Huaifang was a northerner who had brought Yi li and Li ji commentaries from Wei and kept them secret. When he was dying he told his family, "After my death, if Student Qi comes, give him the Yi li and Li ji texts; if he does not come, bury them with me."

sentences.zh: 其為儒者推許如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which Confucians held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which Confucians held him.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太學博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made erudite of the grand academy.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，召羇講論。

translations.literal: When Jianwen was crown prince, he summoned Ji to lecture and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince, he summoned Ji to lecture.

sentences.zh: 又嘗置宴集玄儒之士，先命道學互相質難，次令中庶子徐摛馳騁大義，間以劇談。

translations.literal: He also once gave a banquet gathering profound Confucians, first ordering Daoist scholars to question one another, then ordering Central Palace Attendant Xu Chi to range through great principles with sharp talk interspersed.
translations.idiomatic: He also once gave a banquet for profound Confucians, first ordering Daoist scholars to debate one another, then ordering central palace attendant Xu Chi to range through great principles with sharp talk.

sentences.zh: 摛辭辯縱橫，難以答抗，諸人懾氣，皆失次序。

translations.literal: Chi's rhetoric was fluent and hard to answer; all were overawed and lost their order.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's rhetoric was fluent and hard to answer; all were overawed and lost their composure.

sentences.zh: 羇時騁義，〔一三〕摛與往復，羇精采自若，對答如流，簡文深加歎賞。

translations.literal: Ji then ranged through the meanings [13]; he and Chi went back and forth, Ji spirited and at ease, answering like flowing water; Jianwen deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then ranged through the meanings [13]; he and Chi debated back and forth, Ji spirited and at ease, answering like flowing water; Jianwen deeply admired him.

sentences.zh: 尋除員外散騎侍郎，又遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, then promoted to Regular Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry, then promoted to regular extraordinary attendant.

sentences.zh: 敬帝承制，出為江州長史，仍隨沈泰鎮南豫州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing assumed the provisional regime, he went out as Long Marcher of Jiangzhou and followed Shen Tai in garrisoning Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing assumed the provisional regime, Ji went out as long marcher of Jiangzhou and followed Shen Tai in garrisoning Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰之奔齊也，逼羇俱行，後自鄴下遁還。

translations.literal: When Tai fled to Qi he forced Ji to go with him; later Ji escaped back from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai fled to Qi he forced Ji to go with him; later Ji escaped back from Ye.

sentences.zh: 又隨程文季北伐，呂梁軍敗，羇沒于周，久之得歸。

translations.literal: He again followed Cheng Wenji on the northern campaign; when the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Ji was captured by Zhou and only after long time returned.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Cheng Wenji on the northern campaign; when the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Ji was captured by Zhou and only after a long time returned.

sentences.zh: 仍兼國子助教，除中衛始興王府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was again made Erudite Assistant of the Imperial Academy and appointed Recorder of the Prince of Shixing's household in the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made erudite assistant of the imperial academy and appointed recorder of the Prince of Shixing's household in the central guard.

sentences.zh: 太建十三年卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Taijian, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 13 of Taijian, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 羇於梁代撰三禮義記，值亂亡失，禮記義四十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Ji in the Liang age compiled a Recorded Meaning of the Three Rites; it was lost in the turmoil, but his forty-scroll Meaning of the Li ji circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ji in Liang times compiled a Recorded Meaning of the Three Rites, lost in the turmoil; his forty-scroll Meaning of the Li ji circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 鄭灼字茂昭，東陽信安人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was a native of Xin'an in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was from Xin'an in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖惠，梁衡陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Liang Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was Liang administrator of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 父季徽，通直散騎侍郎、建安令。

translations.literal: His father Jihui was Regular Attendant of Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry and Magistrate of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jihui was regular attendant of direct communication of the scattered cavalry and magistrate of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 灼幼而聰敏，勵志儒學，少受業于皇侃。

translations.literal: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted himself to Confucian learning, and in youth received instruction from Huang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was clever and keen from youth, devoted himself to Confucian learning, and studied under Huang Kan.

sentences.zh: 梁中大通五年，釋褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongtong of Liang he was first appointed Court Gentleman for the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 of Zhongtong of Liang he was first appointed court gentleman for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外散騎侍郎、給事中、安東臨川王府記室參軍，轉平西邵陵王府記室。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Attendant at the Imperial Banquets, and Recorder of the Prince of Linchuan's household in Pacify-the-East; he was transferred to Recorder of the Prince of Shaoling's household in Pacify-the-West.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry, attendant at the imperial banquets, and recorder of the Prince of Linchuan's pacify-the-east household, then recorder of the Prince of Shaoling's pacify-the-west household.

sentences.zh: 簡文在東宮，雅愛經術，引灼為西省義學士。

translations.literal: When Jianwen was crown prince he greatly loved the classics and brought Zhuo in as a Meaning Scholar of the Western Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince he loved the classics and brought Zhuo in as a meaning scholar of the western secretariat.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，除通直散騎侍郎，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry and additionally Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he was made regular attendant of direct communication and additionally erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 尋為威戎將軍，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Martial-Resolution General and additionally Attendant for Palace Affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made martial-resolution general and additionally attendant for palace affairs of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖、世祖之世，歷安東臨川、鎮北鄱陽二王府諮議參軍，累遷中散大夫，以本職兼國子博士。

translations.literal: In the ages of Gaozu and Shizu he served as Deliberator in the households of the Princes of Linchuan in Pacify-the-East and Poyang in Pacify-the-North, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Palace Gentlemen, and in his former office was additionally Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu and Shizu he served as deliberator in the households of the princes of Linchuan and Poyang, rose to grand master of palace gentlemen, and in his former office was additionally erudite of the imperial academy.

translations.idiomatic: Before he could take the appointment he died in year 13 of Taijian, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 灼性精勤，尤明三禮。

translations.literal: Zhuo by nature was diligent and especially clear in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was by nature diligent and especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 少時嘗夢與皇侃遇於途，侃謂灼曰「鄭郎開口」，侃因唾灼口中，自後義理逾進。

translations.literal: In youth he once dreamed of meeting Huang Kan on the road; Kan said to Zhuo, "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth," and Kan spat into Zhuo's mouth; from then on his grasp of principles advanced further.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he dreamed of meeting Huang Kan on the road; Kan said, "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth," and spat into Zhuo's mouth; from then on his grasp of principles advanced further.

sentences.zh: 灼家貧，抄義疏以日繼夜，筆毫盡，每削用之。

translations.literal: Zhuo's family was poor; he copied commentaries day into night, and when brush tips were worn out he would shave them for reuse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's family was poor; he copied commentaries day into night, and when brush tips wore out he shaved them for reuse.

sentences.zh: 灼常蔬食，講授多苦心熱，若瓜時，輒偃臥以瓜鎮心，起便誦讀，其篤志如此。

translations.literal: Zhuo often ate vegetables; lecturing often brought heart heat; in melon season he would lie down and use melon to calm his heart, then rise and recite at once—such was his devoted will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo often ate vegetables; lecturing often brought heart heat; in melon season he would lie down with melon to calm his heart, then rise and recite at once—such was his devotion.

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ya and Lu Xu

translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Ya of Jinling, Lu Xu of Wu, Shen Dewei of Wuxing, and He Deji of Kuaiji all styled themselves masters of ritual learning.

translations.idiomatic: Lu Xu in youth studied Cui Ling'en's lineage of meaning in the Three Rites; in Liang times Baekje requested an erudite to lecture on the rites, and an edict ordered Xu to go.

sentences.zh: 還除給事中、定陽令。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Attendant at the Imperial Banquets and Magistrate of Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made attendant at the imperial banquets and magistrate of Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，侍始興王伯茂讀，遷尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he attended Prince Bomao of Shixing in study and was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjia he attended Prince Bomao of Shixing in study and was promoted to director of the masters of writing for the rites bureau.

sentences.zh: 沈德威

translations.literal: Shen Dewei
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dewei

translations.literal: He Deji
translations.idiomatic: He Deji

sentences.zh: 賀德基字承業，世傳禮學。

translations.literal: He Deji, styled Chengye, transmitted ritual learning through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: He Deji, styled Chengye, transmitted ritual learning through the generations.

sentences.zh: 祖文發，父淹，仕梁俱為祠部郎，並有名當世。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan both served Liang as Directors of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau and were famed in their age.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan both served Liang as directors of the masters of writing for the rites bureau and were famed in their age.

translations.literal: Deji in youth traveled to study in the capital; for years he did not return, clothing and funds were exhausted, and he was ashamed to wear old and worn garments—in deep winter he wore only a lined jacket and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Deji in youth studied in the capital; for years he did not return, his clothing and funds were exhausted, and he was ashamed to wear old garments—in deep winter he wore only a lined jacket and trousers.

translations.idiomatic: He once met a woman before White Horse Temple in splendid dress; she called Deji into the temple gate and gave him her white silk headcloth.

translations.idiomatic: She then said to Deji, "You are about to become a great vessel; soon you will not be poor and cold, so I give you this.

translations.literal: " Deji asked the old woman's name; she did not answer and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Deji asked the old woman's name; she did not answer and left.

sentences.zh: 德基於禮記稱為精明，居以傳授，累遷尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Deji in the Li ji was called penetratingly clear; he lived by transmitting instruction and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Deji was called penetratingly clear in the Li ji; he lived by teaching and rose to director of the masters of writing for the rites bureau.

sentences.zh: 德基雖不至大官，而三世儒學，俱為祠部，時論美其不墜焉。

translations.literal: Although Deji did not reach high office, three generations of Confucian learning all held the Rites Bureau, and opinion of the time praised that the line did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Although Deji did not reach high office, three generations of Confucian learning all held the rites bureau, and opinion praised that the line did not fall.

translations.literal: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
