translations.literal: In youth he received the Changes from Erudite Chu Zhongdu, devoted himself to study and play, and obtained its subtle points.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Changes under erudite Chu Zhongdu, devoted himself to study, and obtained its subtle points.

sentences.zh: 梁太清初，歷王國侍郎、奉朝請，俄轉國子助教，兼司義郎，專講詩、易。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing of Liang he served as Gentleman of the Princely Household and Court Gentleman for the Dynasty; soon he was made Erudite Assistant of the Imperial Academy and additionally Director of Meanings, specializing in lecturing on the Odes and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing of Liang he served as gentleman of the princely household and court gentleman; soon he was made erudite assistant and additionally director of meanings, specializing in the Odes and Changes.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，除尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was made Director of the Masters of Writing for the Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In year 1 of Shaotai he was made director of the masters of writing for the water bureau.

sentences.zh: 太建中，累遷〔鎮〕南始興王府諮議參軍，〔一四〕隨府詣湘州，以疾卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was repeatedly promoted to Deliberator in the Pacify-South household of the Prince of Shixing [14]; he followed the princely establishment to Xiangzhou and died of illness, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he rose to deliberator in the pacify-south household of the Prince of Shixing [14]; he followed the establishment to Xiangzhou and died of illness, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 緩治周易、老、莊，時人言玄者咸推之。

translations.literal: Huan mastered the Zhou yi, Lao zi, and Zhuang zi; among those who spoke of the arcane he was universally praised.
translations.idiomatic: Huan mastered the Zhou yi, Lao zi, and Zhuang zi; among those who spoke of the arcane he was universally praised.

sentences.zh: 張譏字直言，清河武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was from Wucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖僧寶，梁散騎侍郎、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Grandfather Sengbao was Liang attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbao was Liang attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 父仲悅，梁廬陵王府錄事參軍、尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Father Zhongyue was Liang recording adviser to the Prince of Luling's household and bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongyue was Liang recording adviser to the prince of Luling's household and bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 譏幼聰俊，有思理，年十四，通孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Ji from youth was clever and sharp, with thoughtful discernment; at age fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was clever and sharp from youth, with thoughtful discernment; at fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 篤好玄言，受學于汝南周弘正，每有新意，為先輩推伏。

translations.literal: He deeply loved dark learning, studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan, and whenever he had a fresh insight elders acknowledged and deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply loved xuanxue, studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan, and whenever he had a fresh insight the elders deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，召補國子正言生。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Liang he was summoned and appointed regular student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era he was summoned as a regular student of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘗於文德殿釋乾、坤文言，譏與陳郡袁憲等預焉，敕令論譏，諸儒莫敢先出，譏乃整容而進，諮審循環，辭令溫雅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once at Wendé Hall explained the Wenyan sections of Qian and Kun; Ji together with Yuan Xian of Chen commandery and others were present. An edict ordered debate; none of the scholars dared speak first. Ji composed himself and advanced, inquiry and examination going round and round, his words warm and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang once explained the Wenyan on Qian and Kun at Wendé Hall; Ji was there with Yuan Xian of Chen commandery and others. An edict ordered debate, but none of the scholars dared speak first. Ji composed himself and advanced; inquiry went round and round, his words warm and refined.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝甚異之，賜裙襦絹等，仍云「表卿稽古之力」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was greatly struck, granted skirts, robes, silk and the like, and said, "This shows your power in examining antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was greatly struck, granted skirts, robes, and silk, and said, "This shows your power in examining antiquity."

sentences.zh: 譏幼喪母，有錯綵經帕，即母之遺製，及有所識，家人具以告之，每歲時輒對帕哽噎，不能自勝。

translations.literal: Ji lost his mother young; there was a patched colorful sutra cloth—his mother's handiwork. When he came to understand, the household told him fully; each year at the season he would choke over the cloth, unable to master himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ji lost his mother young. There was a patched colorful sutra cloth his mother had made; when he came to understand, the household told him. Each year at the season he would choke over the cloth, unable to master himself.

sentences.zh: 及丁父憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning came due, his observance exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning came due, his observance exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 服闋，召補湘東王國左常侍，轉田曹參軍，遷士林館學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as left regular attendant of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, transferred to field-office adviser, and promoted to scholar of the Forest of Gentlemen hall.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as left regular attendant in the prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, transferred to field-office adviser, and made a scholar of the Forest of Gentlemen hall.

sentences.zh: 簡文在東宮，出士林館發孝經題，譏論議往復，甚見嗟賞，自是每有講集，必遣使召譏。

translations.literal: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he issued from the Forest of Gentlemen a topic on the Classic of Filial Piety; Ji's back-and-forth discourse won high praise, and from then on whenever there was a lecture gathering messengers were always sent to summon Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he issued a topic on the Classic of Filial Piety from the Forest of Gentlemen; Ji's back-and-forth discourse won high praise, and from then on every lecture gathering sent for him.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇逆，於圍城之中，猶侍哀太子於武德後殿講老、莊。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, even within the besieged city he still attended the Lament-heir at Wude rear hall lecturing on Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, even within the besieged city he still attended the lament-heir at Wude rear hall to lecture on Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 梁臺陷，譏崎嶇避難，卒不事景。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime fell, Ji took a rugged path fleeing danger and in the end never served Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime fell, Ji fled by a rugged path and never served Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，歷臨安令。

translations.literal: After Jing was pacified, he served in succession as magistrate of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was pacified, he served in turn as magistrate of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，除太常丞，轉始興王府刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was made vice director of the court for imperial sacrifices, then transferred to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Shixing's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication he was made vice director of the court for imperial sacrifices, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Shixing's household.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，遷國子助教。

translations.literal: In the Tianchen era he was moved to assistant teacher of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianchen era he was made assistant teacher of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 是時周弘正在國學，發周易題，弘正第四弟弘直亦在講席。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Hongzheng was at the national academy and issued a topic on the Book of Changes; Hongzheng's fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the lecture seat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhou Hongzheng was at the national academy and issued a topic on the Book of Changes; his fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the lecture seat.

sentences.zh: 譏與弘正論議，弘正乃屈，弘直危坐厲聲，助其申理。

translations.literal: Ji debated with Hongzheng; Hongzheng was thus subdued. Hongzhi sat upright and raised his voice to help state his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Ji debated with Hongzheng until Hongzheng yielded. Hongzhi sat upright and raised his voice to help state his case.

sentences.zh: 譏乃正色謂弘直曰：「今日義集，辯正名理，雖知兄弟急難，四公不得有助。

translations.literal: Ji then with stern countenance said to Hongzhi: "Today's righteous gathering debates and corrects principles; though one knows brothers rush to each other's aid, you, fourth sir, may not assist."
translations.idiomatic: Ji then said sternly to Hongzhi, "Today's gathering debates principles. Though brothers rush to each other's aid, you, fourth sir, may not help."

sentences.zh: 」弘直曰：「僕助君師，何為不可？

translations.literal: Hongzhi said, "I assist my master's master—why not?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi said, "I assist my master's master—why not?"

sentences.zh: 」舉座以為笑樂。

translations.literal: The whole assembly took it as mirth.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly laughed.

sentences.zh: 弘正嘗謂人曰：「吾每登座，見張譏在席，使人懍然。

translations.literal: Hongzheng once told others: "Whenever I mount the seat and see Zhang Ji in the hall, it makes one stand in awe."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng once said, "Whenever I mount the seat and see Zhang Ji in the hall, it makes one stand in awe."

sentences.zh: 」高宗世，歷建安王府記室參軍，兼東宮學士，轉武陵王限內記室，學士如故。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Gaozong he served in succession as recording secretary to the Prince of Jian'an's household, concurrently eastern-palace scholar, then transferred to recording secretary within the limits for the Prince of Wuling—scholar as before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was recording secretary to the prince of Jian'an's household and eastern-palace scholar, then recording secretary within the limits for the prince of Wuling, still a scholar.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，集官僚置宴，時造玉柄麈尾新成，後主親執之，曰：「當今雖復多士如林，至於堪捉此者，獨張譏耳。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler was in the Eastern Palace he gathered officials for a banquet; a new jade-handled fly-whisk had just been made. The Later Ruler held it himself and said, "Though today scholars are again thick as a forest, as to who can wield this—only Zhang Ji."
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was crown prince he gathered officials for a banquet. A new jade-handled fly-whisk had just been made; he held it and said, "Though scholars today are thick as a forest, only Zhang Ji can wield this."

sentences.zh: 」即手授譏。

translations.literal: He thereupon handed it to Ji in person.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon handed it to Ji in person.

sentences.zh: 仍令於溫文殿講莊、老，高宗幸宮臨聽，賜御所服衣一襲。

translations.literal: He then had him lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi at Wenwen Hall; Emperor Gaozong visited the palace to listen and granted one suit of his own robes.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Ji lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi at Wenwen Hall; Emperor Gaozong visited the palace to listen and granted one suit of his own robes.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，領南平王府諮議參軍、東宮學士。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler succeeded he headed advising secretary to the Prince of Nanping's household and eastern-palace scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler succeeded he was advising secretary to the prince of Nanping's household and eastern-palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 尋遷國子博士，學士如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to erudite of the Imperial University; scholar as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made erudite of the imperial university, still a scholar.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗幸鍾山開善寺召從臣坐於寺西南松林下，敕召譏豎義。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhongshan, summoned followers to sit in the pine grove southwest of the temple, and ordered Ji summoned to set forth the doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhongshan, had his followers sit in the pine grove southwest of the temple, and ordered Ji to set forth the doctrine.

sentences.zh: 時索麈尾未至，後主敕取松枝，手以屬譏，曰「可代麈尾」。

translations.literal: When the sought fly-whisk had not arrived, the Later Ruler ordered a pine branch taken and with his hand gave it to Ji, saying "It can replace the fly-whisk."
translations.idiomatic: When the fly-whisk had not arrived, the Later Ruler ordered a pine branch taken and gave it to Ji, saying, "It can replace the fly-whisk."

sentences.zh: 顧謂群臣曰「此即是張譏後事」。

translations.literal: Turning to the assembled ministers he said, "This is Zhang Ji's business for afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the ministers he said, "This is Zhang Ji's business hereafter."

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入隋，終於長安，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered Sui and died at Chang'an, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and died at Chang'an, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 譏性恬靜，不求榮利，常慕閑逸，所居宅營山池，植花果，講周易、老、莊而教授焉。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was tranquil; he sought no glory or profit and often yearned for leisure. His residence had hills and pools laid out, flowers and fruit planted; there he lectured on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was tranquil by nature and sought no glory or profit, often yearning for leisure. His residence had hills and pools and flowers and fruit; there he lectured on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳郡陸元朗、朱孟博、一乘寺沙門法才、法雲寺沙門慧休、〔一五〕至真觀道士姚綏，皆傳其業。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanlang of Wu commandery, Zhu Mengbo, the monk Facai of Yicheng Temple, the monk Huixiu of Fayun Temple, [15] and the Daoist priest Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey—all transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanlang of Wu commandery, Zhu Mengbo, the monk Facai of Yicheng Temple, the monk Huixiu of Fayun Temple, [15] and the Daoist priest Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey—all transmitted his learning.

sentences.zh: 譏所撰周易義三十卷，尚書義十五卷，毛詩義二十卷，孝經義八卷，論語義二十卷，老子義十一卷，莊子內篇義十二卷，外篇義二十卷，雜篇義十卷，玄部通義十二卷，又撰遊玄桂林二十四卷，後主嘗敕人就其家寫入祕閣。

translations.literal: Works Ji composed: Meaning of the Zhou Changes 30 juan, Meaning of the Documents 15, Meaning of the Mao Odes 20, Meaning of the Filial Classic 8, Meaning of the Analects 20, Meaning of Laozi 11, Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi 12, Outer Chapters 20, Miscellaneous Chapters 10, Comprehensive Meaning of the Mystic Canon 12; he also composed Roaming the Mystic Cassia Grove 24. The Later Ruler once ordered someone to copy them from his home into the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote Meaning of the Zhou Changes in 30 juan, Meaning of the Documents in 15, Meaning of the Mao Odes in 20, Meaning of the Filial Classic in 8, Meaning of the Analects in 20, Meaning of Laozi in 11, Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi in 12, Outer Chapters in 20, Miscellaneous Chapters in 10, and Comprehensive Meaning of the Mystic Canon in 12; he also wrote Roaming the Mystic Cassia Grove in 24. The Later Ruler once ordered them copied from his home into the secret archive.

sentences.zh: 子孝則，官至始安王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozhe rose to recording secretary to the Prince of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhe rose to recording secretary to the prince of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 顧越字思南，〔一六〕吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yue, styled Sinan, [16] was a native of Yanguan in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yue, styled Sinan, [16] was from Yanguan in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 所居新坡黃岡，世有鄉校，由是顧氏多儒學焉。

translations.literal: Where he lived was Xinpo Huangang; for generations there had been a village school, and thus the Gu clan had many Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Xinpo Huangang, where for generations there had been a village school; thus the Gu clan produced many Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 時有東陽龔孟舒者，亦治毛氏詩，善談名理。

translations.literal: At the time there was Gong Mengshu of Dongyang, who also studied the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gong Mengshu of Dongyang also studied the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.

sentences.zh: 梁武世，仕至尋陽郡丞，元帝在江州，遇之甚重，躬師事焉。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Wu of Liang he rose to assistant magistrate of Xunyang commandery; when Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he esteemed him greatly and personally took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Liang he rose to assistant magistrate of Xunyang; when Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he esteemed him greatly and took him as teacher in person.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era he concurrently served as palace scribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he concurrently served as palace scribe.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，除員外散騎常侍，兼國子助教、太中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, concurrently assistant teacher of the Imperial University and grand master for supervision of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, concurrently assistant teacher of the imperial university and grand master for supervision of the army.

sentences.zh: 太建中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Taijian era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Taijian era.

sentences.zh: 沈不害

translations.literal: Shen Buhai
translations.idiomatic: Shen Buhai

sentences.zh: 沈不害字孝和，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖總，齊尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zong was Qi director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zong was Qi director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 父懿，梁邵陵王參軍。

translations.literal: Father Yi was a Liang staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was a Liang staff officer to the prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 不害幼孤，而脩立好學。

translations.literal: Buhai was orphaned young yet cultivated himself and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai was orphaned young yet cultivated himself and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 十四，召補國子生，舉明經。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was summoned as student of the Imperial University and nominated for mastery of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was summoned as a student of the imperial university and nominated for mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 累遷梁太學博士，轉廬陵王府刑獄參軍，長沙王府諮議，帶汝南令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Liang grand-academy doctor, then transferred to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Luling's household, advising secretary to the Prince of Changsha, and concurrently magistrate of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Liang grand-academy doctor, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Luling's household, advising secretary to the prince of Changsha, and concurrently magistrate of Runan.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，除衡陽王府中記室參軍，兼嘉德殿學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made middle recording secretary to the Prince of Hengyang's household and concurrently scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made middle recording secretary to the prince of Hengyang's household and scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.

sentences.zh: 自梁季喪亂，至是國學未立，不害上書曰：

translations.literal: From the disorders at the end of Liang until then the national academy had not been established; Buhai submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: From the disorders at the end of Liang until then the national academy had not been established; Buhai submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞立人建國，莫尚於尊儒，成俗化民，必崇於教學。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in establishing persons and founding states, nothing surpasses honoring Confucian scholars; in completing customs and transforming the people, one must exalt teaching and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that in establishing persons and founding states nothing surpasses honoring Confucian scholars, and in completing customs and transforming the people one must exalt teaching and learning.

sentences.zh: 故東膠西序，事隆乎三代，環林璧水，業盛於兩京。

translations.literal: Thus the eastern glue and western school—affairs reached their height in the Three Dynasties; the ringed forest and jade water—the enterprise flourished in the Two Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the eastern glue and western school reached their height in the Three Dynasties, and the ringed forest and jade water flourished in the Two Capitals.

sentences.zh: 自淳源既遠，澆波已扇，物之感人無窮，人之逐欲無節，是以設訓垂範，啟導心靈，譬彼染藍，類諸琢玉，然後人倫以睦，卑高有序，忠孝之理既明，君臣之道攸固。

translations.literal: Since the pure source had grown distant and the shallow wave had already risen, the myriad things' power to move people is inexhaustible and people's pursuit of desire knows no bounds—therefore one sets instruction and hangs models, opens and guides the mind, like dyeing in indigo or like carving jade; only then are human relations made harmonious, high and low given order, the principle of loyalty and filial piety made clear, and the way of ruler and minister made firm.
translations.idiomatic: Since the pure source had grown distant and shallow ways had risen, things move people without end and desire knows no bounds. Therefore one sets instruction and models, opens and guides the mind, like dyeing in indigo or carving jade; only then are human relations harmonious, high and low ordered, loyalty and filial piety clear, and the way of ruler and minister firm.

sentences.zh: 執禮自基，魯公所以難侮，歌樂已細，鄭伯於是前亡，干戚舞而有苗至，泮宮成而淮夷服，長想洙、泗之風，載懷淹、稷之盛，有國有家，莫不尚已。

translations.literal: Taking ritual as foundation—the Duke of Lu was therefore hard to insult; when song and music had grown minute, the Earl of Zheng thereupon perished first; when shield and axes were danced the Miao came; when the pan-palace was completed the Huai Yi submitted—long to think on the wind of Zhu and Si, fully to cherish the flourishing of Yan and Ji: states and families, none but honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Taking ritual as foundation, the Duke of Lu was hard to insult; when song and music grew minute, the Earl of Zheng perished; when shield and axes were danced the Miao came; when the pan-palace was completed the Huai Yi submitted. Long to recall the wind of Zhu and Si and the flourishing of Yan and Ji—states and families all honored it.

sentences.zh: 梁太清季年，數鍾否剝，戎狄外侵，姦回內奰，朝聞鼓鼙，夕炤烽火。

translations.literal: In the last years of Liang's Taiqing era, misfortune repeatedly struck; barbarians invaded from without, wicked factions rebelled within; in the morning drums and gongs were heard, by evening beacon fires shone.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Liang's Taiqing era misfortune struck again and again; barbarians invaded from without and wicked factions rebelled within; drums and gongs were heard in the morning, beacon fires by evening.

sentences.zh: 洪儒碩學，解散甚於坑夷，五典、九丘，湮滅逾乎帷蓋。

translations.literal: Great Confucians and broad scholars were scattered worse than the pit-martyrs; the Five Classics and Nine Sections were effaced more than under a canopy-screen.
translations.idiomatic: Great Confucians and broad scholars were scattered worse than the pit-martyrs; the Five Classics and Nine Sections were lost worse than under a canopy.

sentences.zh: 成均自斯墜業，瞽宗於是不脩，褒成之祠弗陳祼享，釋菜之禮無稱俎豆，頌聲寂莫，遂踰一紀。

translations.literal: The accomplished mean from then cast its work down; the blind-director shrine was thereupon not repaired; the shrine of Bao Cheng offered no libation-sacrifice; the rite of presenting vegetables had no claim on ritual vessels; hymnody fell silent—for more than twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: The accomplished mean then cast down its work; the blind-director shrine went unrepaired; the shrine of Bao Cheng offered no libation; the rite of presenting vegetables had no vessels; hymnody fell silent for more than twelve years.

sentences.zh: 後生敦悅，不見函杖之儀，晚學鑽仰，徒深倚席之歎。

translations.literal: Later students delighted in learning but did not see the ritual of bearing the writing tablet; late scholars drilled and looked up, yet only deepened the sigh of leaning on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Later students delighted in learning but never saw the ritual of bearing the writing tablet; late scholars drilled and looked up, yet only sighed at leaning on the mat.

sentences.zh: 陛下繼曆升統，握鏡臨宇，道洽寰中，威加無外，濁流已清，重氛載廓，含生熙阜，品庶咸亨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has succeeded to the calendar and mounted the throne, holding the mirror and overlooking the realm; the Way has penetrated within the seas, authority extends beyond all borders; turbid currents are already clear, heavy mists are greatly dispersed; the living flourish on high mounds, all ranks enjoy prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and holds the mirror over the realm; the Way fills the seas and authority extends beyond all borders; turbid currents are clear and heavy mists dispersed; the living flourish and all ranks prosper.

sentences.zh: 宜其弘振禮樂，建立庠序，式稽古典，紆跡儒宮，選公卿門子，皆入于學，助教博士，朝夕講肄，使擔簦負笈，鏘鏘接衽，方領矩步，濟濟成林。

translations.literal: It is fitting to grandly revive ritual and music, establish schools and academies, model antiquity's rules, linger with footprints at the Confucian palace, select sons of dukes and ministers—all to enter study; assistant teachers and erudites to lecture morning and evening—so that those who shoulder book-boxes and carry satchels rustle garment to garment, square-collared and measured in step, press thick as a forest.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to revive ritual and music grandly, establish schools, model antiquity, and dwell at the Confucian palace, selecting sons of dukes and ministers for study, with assistant teachers and erudites lecturing morning and evening, so that those who shoulder book-boxes and carry satchels press thick as a forest, square-collared and measured in step.

sentences.zh: 如切如磋，聞詩聞禮，一年可以功倍，三冬於是足用。

translations.literal: As if cutting, as if polishing; hearing the Odes, hearing the Rites—one year can double the work; three winters then suffice for use.
translations.idiomatic: As if cutting, as if polishing; hearing the Odes and Rites—one year doubles the work, three winters suffice for use.

sentences.zh: 故能擢秀雄州，揚庭觀國，入仕登朝，資優學以自輔，蒞官從政，有經業以治身，轖駕列庭，青紫拾地。

translations.literal: Thus one can raise excellence in a commandery, raise one's name in court and observe the state; enter office and ascend court, relying on superior learning to aid oneself; take office and govern, having classic learning to order the person—carriages fill the court, blue and purple are gathered from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one can raise excellence in a commandery and one's name at court; enter office and ascend court aided by superior learning; take office and govern with classic learning to order the person—carriages fill the court and blue and purple are gathered from the ground.

sentences.zh: 古者王世子之貴，猶與國子齒，降及漢儲，茲禮不墜，暨乎兩晉，斯事彌隆，所以見師嚴而道尊者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the crown prince's nobility still ranked with the sons of the state; down to the Han heir this ritual did not fall; reaching the two Jin, this matter grew even more exalted—thus one sees the teacher honored and the Way respected.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the crown prince's nobility still ranked with the sons of the state; down to the Han heir this ritual did not fall; in the two Jin it grew more exalted—thus the teacher is honored and the Way respected.

sentences.zh: 皇太子天縱生知，無待審喻，猶宜晦跡俯同，專經請業，奠爵前師，肅若舊典。

translations.literal: The crown prince is heaven-bestowed with innate knowledge and needs no repeated explanation—yet he should still conceal his traces and bow level with others, specialize in the classics and request instruction, set forth the libation cup before the teacher, solemn as the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is heaven-bestowed with innate knowledge and needs no repeated explanation, yet he should still bow level with others, specialize in the classics and request instruction, and set forth the libation cup before the teacher, solemn as the old canon.

sentences.zh: 昔闕里之堂，莫萊自辟，舊宅之內，絲竹流音，前聖遺烈，深以炯戒。

translations.literal: Formerly in the hall at Que Li, Mo Lai opened his own path; within the old dwelling, silk and bamboo streamed with sound—the former sage's legacy warns sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the hall at Que Li, Mo Lai opened his own path; within the old dwelling silk and bamboo streamed—the former sage's legacy warns sharply.

sentences.zh: 況復江表無虞，海外有截，豈得不開闡大猷，恢弘至道？

translations.literal: Moreover the lands south of the Yangtze are without care, beyond the seas are cut off—how can one fail to open and spread the great plan, extend and magnify the utmost Way?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the lands south of the Yangtze are secure and the seas are cut off—how can one fail to open the great plan and extend the utmost Way?

sentences.zh: 寧可使玄教儒風，弗興聖世，盛德大業，遂蘊堯年？

translations.literal: Could one allow the dark teaching and Confucian wind not to rise in a sage age, great virtue and great enterprise to lie hidden in Yao's years?
translations.idiomatic: Could one allow the dark teaching and Confucian wind not to rise in a sage age, or great virtue and great enterprise to lie hidden like Yao's years?

sentences.zh: 臣末學小生，詞無足筭，輕獻瞽言，伏增悚惕。

translations.literal: Your servant, a petty late student, words not worth reckoning, lightly offers blind words and increases dread bowed low.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, a petty late student whose words are not worth reckoning, lightly offers blind counsel and bows in dread.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「省表聞之。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Your memorial has been read."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Your memorial has been read."

sentences.zh: 自舊章弛廢，微言將絕，朕嗣膺寶業，念在緝熙，而兵革未息，軍國草創，常恐前王令典，一朝泯滅。

translations.literal: "Since old regulations were relaxed and abandoned, subtle words were about to perish; We have succeeded to the precious enterprise and Our thought is in drawing brightness close—yet arms have not ceased and army and state are still newly founded; We constantly fear the former kings' ordered canon may in a morning be extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: "Since old regulations were abandoned, subtle words were about to perish. We have succeeded to the precious enterprise and seek to draw brightness close, yet arms have not ceased and army and state are still newly founded; We constantly fear the former kings' ordered canon may be extinguished in a morning."

sentences.zh: 卿才思優洽，文理可求，弘惜大體，殷勤名教，付外詳議，依事施行。

translations.literal: "Your talent and thought are excellent and harmonious, your wen and li can be sought; broadly cherish the great body, earnestly attend the teaching of names—deliver to outside for detailed deliberation and implement according to affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "Your talent and thought are excellent, your wen and li can be sought; broadly cherish the great body and earnestly attend the teaching of names—deliver outside for detailed deliberation and implement according to affairs."

sentences.zh: 又表改定樂章，詔使製三朝樂歌八首，合二十八曲，行之樂府。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to revise and fix ritual hymns; an edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty-eight pieces in all, implemented at the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to revise ritual hymns; an edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty-eight pieces in all, for the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 五年，除灨令。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was made magistrate of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made magistrate of Gan.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書儀曹郎，遷國子博士，領羽林監，敕治五禮，掌策文謚議。

translations.literal: He entered service as bureau director of ceremonies in the masters of writing, was moved to erudite of the Imperial University, headed the Feathered Forest guard, was ordered to compile the five rites, and managed draft texts for posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as bureau director of ceremonies in the masters of writing, became erudite of the imperial university, headed the feathered forest guard, was ordered to compile the five rites, and managed draft texts for posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 太建中，除仁武南康嗣王府長史，行丹陽郡事。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he was made chief steward to the Prince of Renwu, heir of Nan and Kang, and acted in the affairs of Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was chief steward to the prince of Renwu, heir of Nan and Kang, and acted in Danyang affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍、光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and minister of the household for the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and minister of the household for the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 尋為戎昭將軍、明威武陵王長史，行吳興郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made martial-proclamation general and chief steward to the Prince of Mingwu in Wuling, acting in the affairs of Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was martial-proclamation general and chief steward to the prince of Mingwu in Wuling, acting in Wuxing affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄入為通直散騎常侍，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Shortly he entered service as attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication and concurrently left assistant in the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he entered service as attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication and left assistant in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In year 12 he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 不害治經術，善屬文，雖博綜墳典，而家無卷軸。

translations.literal: Buhai mastered classic learning and excelled at composition; though broadly versed in the canonical tomes, his home had no scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai mastered the classics and excelled at composition; though broadly versed in the canonical tomes, his home had no scrolls.

sentences.zh: 每製文，操筆立成，曾無尋檢。

translations.literal: Whenever he composed a text he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to search or check.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he composed he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to search or check.

sentences.zh: 僕射汝南周弘正常稱之曰：「沈生可謂意聖人乎！

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhou Hongzheng of Runan always praised him, saying: "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas!
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Zhou Hongzheng of Runan always said, "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas!

sentences.zh: 」著治五禮儀一百卷，文集十四卷。

translations.literal: " He authored Correcting the Five Rites Protocols in one hundred juan and a collected writings in fourteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote Correcting the Five Rites Protocols in one hundred juan and collected writings in fourteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子志道，字崇基，少知名。

translations.literal: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth.

sentences.zh: 解褐揚州主簿，尋兼文林著士，歷安東新蔡王記室參軍。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was registrar of Yangzhou; soon he concurrently served as Palace Forest scholar and in succession was recording secretary to the Prince of Andong in Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was registrar of Yangzhou; soon he was also a Palace Forest scholar and recording secretary to the prince of Andong in Xin.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入隋。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui.

sentences.zh: 王元規

translations.literal: Wang Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuangui

sentences.zh: 王元規字正範，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖道寶，〔二０〕齊員外散騎常侍、晉安郡守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Daobao, [20] was Qi supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Jin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daobao, [20] was Qi supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Jin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父瑋，梁武陵王府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: Father Wei was middle recording secretary to the Prince of Wuling's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei was middle recording secretary to the prince of Wuling's household.

sentences.zh: 元規八歲而孤，兄弟三人，隨母依舅氏往臨海郡，時年十二。

translations.literal: Yuangui was orphaned at eight; three brothers followed their mother to rely on a maternal uncle's clan and went to Linhai commandery when he was twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was orphaned at eight; he and his two brothers followed their mother to their uncle's house in Linhai commandery when he was twelve.

sentences.zh: 郡土豪劉瑱者，資財巨萬，以女妻之。

translations.literal: A local magnate of the commandery, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and offered his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 元規母以其兄弟幼弱，欲結彊援，元規泣請曰：「姻不失親，〔二一〕古人所重。

translations.literal: Yuangui's mother, because the brothers were young and weak, wished to secure a powerful ally; Yuangui wept and pleaded, saying: "Marriage must not lose kin—[21] ancients held it weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui's mother, because the brothers were young, wished to secure a powerful ally; Yuangui wept and pleaded, "Marriage must not lose kin—[21] ancients held it weighty.

sentences.zh: 豈得苟安異壤，輒婚非類！

translations.literal: How can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind!
translations.idiomatic: How can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind!

sentences.zh: 」母感其言而止。

translations.literal: " His mother was moved by his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother was moved and stopped.

sentences.zh: 元規性孝，事母甚謹，晨昏未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care; morning and evening he never left her side.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care, never leaving her side morning or evening.

sentences.zh: 梁時山陰縣有暴水，流漂居宅，元規唯有一小船，倉卒引其母妹并孤姪入船，〔二二〕元規自執楫棹而去，留其男女三人，閣於樹杪，及水退獲全，時人皆稱其至行。

translations.literal: In Liang times Shanyin county had a sudden flood that swept away the dwelling; Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephews into the boat, [22] while Yuangui himself took the oars and went off, leaving three male and female kin lodged in the treetops; when the water receded all were saved, and people of the time all praised his utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang times a sudden flood in Shanyin swept away their dwelling; Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste put his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephews aboard, [22] while he himself took the oars and went off, leaving three kin lodged in the treetops; when the water receded all were saved, and people praised his utmost conduct.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，引為學士，親受禮記、左傳、喪服等義，賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler was in the Eastern Palace he was summoned as scholar; he personally received instruction in the meanings of the Record of Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Mourning Garments, with generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was crown prince he was summoned as scholar and personally received instruction in the Record of Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Mourning Garments, with generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 新安王伯固嘗因入宮適會元規將講，乃啟請執經，時論以為榮。

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace and happened upon Yuangui about to lecture; he petitioned to hold the classics, and contemporary opinion deemed it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace just as Yuangui was about to lecture and petitioned to hold the classics; opinion at the time took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 俄除尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Master of Writing in the Bureau of Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed master of writing in the bureau of temples.

sentences.zh: 自梁代諸儒相傳為左氏學者，皆以賈逵、服虔之義難駮杜預，凡一百八十條，元規引證通析，無復疑滯。

translations.literal: Since Liang times Confucians who transmitted the Zuo tradition had all used Jia Kui and Fu Qian's interpretations to challenge Du Yu—one hundred eighty items in all—Yuangui cited and analyzed them until no doubts remained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang, Zuo-tradition scholars had used Jia Kui and Fu Qian to challenge Du Yu in 180 points; Yuangui cited and analyzed them until nothing was left in doubt.

sentences.zh: 每國家議吉凶大禮，常參預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the state deliberated on auspicious and inauspicious great rites, he regularly took part.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state debated great rites of fortune and misfortune, he regularly took part.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去職，服闋，除鄱陽王府中錄事參軍，俄轉散騎侍郎，遷南平王府限內參軍。

translations.literal: On mother's mourning he left office; when mourning ended, he was made Recorder of the Prince of Poyang's household, soon transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and advanced to Limited Attendant in the Prince of Nanping's household.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he left office; when mourning ended he became recorder in the prince of Poyang's household, soon regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then limited attendant in the prince of Nanping's household.

sentences.zh: 王為江州，元規隨府之鎮，四方學徒，不遠千里來請道者，常數十百人。

translations.literal: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the prefectural staff; students from all directions came from afar to seek the Way—often several tens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the staff; students from every quarter came a thousand li to seek instruction—often scores or hundreds at a time.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入隋，為秦王府東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and was made Eastern Pavilion Sacrificial Wine to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and became eastern-pavilion sacrificial wine to the prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，卒於廣陵。

translations.literal: At age seventy-four he died at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-four he died at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 元規著春秋發題辭及義記十一卷，〔二三〕續經典大義十四卷，孝經義記兩卷，左傳音三卷，禮記音兩卷。

translations.literal: Yuangui authored eleven scrolls of Spring and Autumn Opening Topics and Expository Records, [23] fourteen scrolls continuing Classic Great Meanings, two scrolls of Expository Records on the Classic of Filial Piety, three scrolls of Notes on Zuo's Sounds, and two scrolls of Notes on the Rites' Sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui wrote eleven scrolls of Spring and Autumn opening topics and expository records, [23] fourteen scrolls continuing classic great meanings, two on the Classic of Filial Piety, three on Zuo's sounds, and two on the Rites' sounds.

sentences.zh: 子大業，聰敏知名。

translations.literal: His son Daye was clever and famed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daye was clever and well known.

sentences.zh: 時有吳郡陸慶，少好學，遍知五經，尤明春秋左氏傳，節操甚高。

translations.literal: At the time Wu commandery's Lu Qing from youth loved study, fully knew the Five Classics, especially excelled in Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and had very high integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lu Qing of Wu commandery had loved learning from youth, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially expert in Zuo's Commentary, with very high integrity.

sentences.zh: 釋褐梁武陵王國右常侍，歷征西府墨曹行參軍，除婁令。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was Right Ordinary Attendant in the Prince of Wuling's Liang kingdom; he served as Acting Aide in the Ink Bureau of the Campaign-West headquarters and was appointed magistrate of Lou.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was right ordinary attendant in the prince of Wuling's Liang kingdom, served as acting aide in the campaign-west ink bureau, and was appointed magistrate of Lou.

sentences.zh: 值梁季喪亂，乃覃心釋典，經論靡不該究。

translations.literal: When Liang's end brought turmoil, he devoted his mind to Buddhist sutras; no sutra or treatise escaped his study.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell into turmoil he turned his mind to Buddhist sutras and mastered every sutra and treatise.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，徵為通直散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: Early in Tianchen he was summoned as Undifferentiated Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianchen he was summoned as undifferentiated attendant of the scattered cavalry but declined.

sentences.zh: 永陽王為吳郡太守，聞其名，欲與相見，慶固辭以疾。

translations.literal: Prince Yongyang as Wu commandery administrator heard his fame and wished to meet him; Qing firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongyang, as Wu commandery administrator, heard of him and wished to meet; Qing firmly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 時宗人陸榮為郡五官掾，慶嘗詣焉，王乃微服往榮第，穿壁以觀之。

translations.literal: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's Five Offices aide; Qing once visited him, and the prince went in disguise to Rong's residence and peered through a wall to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's five-offices aide; when Qing visited him, the prince went in disguise to Rong's house and watched through a wall.

sentences.zh: 王謂榮曰：「觀陸慶風神凝峻，殆不可測，嚴君平、鄭子真何以尚茲。

translations.literal: The prince told Rong: "Observing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he can hardly be fathomed; how could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be set above this?
translations.idiomatic: The prince told Rong, "Seeing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he is hardly fathomable; how could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be ranked above him?

sentences.zh: 」鄱陽、晉安王俱以記室徵，並不就。

translations.literal: " The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: " The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 乃築室屏居，以禪誦為事，由是傳經受業者蓋鮮焉。

translations.literal: He then built a dwelling in seclusion and took chanting meditation as his business; hence those transmitting the classics and receiving instruction became rare indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a secluded dwelling and made chanting meditation his occupation; from then on those who transmitted the classics and took pupils were few indeed.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫砥身勵行，必先經術，樹國崇家，率由茲道，故王政因之而至治，人倫得之而攸序。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: To hone the person and exhort conduct, one must first have classical learning; to establish the state and honor the family, all follow this path—thus royal government through it attains perfect order, and human relations through it find their proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: To hone the person and exhort conduct one must first master the classics; to establish the state and honor the family all follow this path—thus royal government through it reaches good order, and human relations through it keep their proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 若沈文阿之徒，各專經授業，亦一代之鴻儒焉。

translations.literal: Men like Shen Wena, each specializing in the classics and transmitting instruction, were also great Confucians of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Shen Wena, each devoted to the classics and teaching pupils, were great Confucians of their generation as well.

sentences.zh: 文阿加復草創禮儀，蓋叔孫通之流亞矣。

translations.literal: Wena moreover drafted rites in their first inception—he was nearly of Shusun Tong's kind.
translations.idiomatic: Wena moreover helped draft rites at their inception—he was nearly in Shusun Tong's class.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 〔一〕 斯則王教之典籍先聖所以明天道 北監本、殿本作「以教之典籍，斯則先聖所以明天道」。

translations.literal: [1] "then the kingly teaching's canon scriptures whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "the teaching's canon scriptures, then whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: On "then the kingly teaching's canon scriptures whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "the teaching's canon scriptures, then whereby the former sages illuminate Heaven's Way."

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2.
translations.idiomatic: Note 2.

translations.literal: (opening)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (opening).

sentences.zh: 〔置〕弟子員 據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [establish] student slots—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[establish] student slots": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 總以五經教授

translations.literal: [3] "overall to instruct with the five classics"
translations.idiomatic: On "[3] overall to instruct with the five classics"

sentences.zh: （唯國學乃經）

translations.literal: (only the National University then classics)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (only the National University then classics).

sentences.zh: 經各置助教云 據北監本、殿本刪。

translations.literal: each classic had its own assistant instructor, etc.—deleted according to the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "each classic had its own assistant instructor": deleted per the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 按南史儒林傳序亦無此五字。

translations.literal: Note: the Southern History preface to the Confucian Scholars biography also lacks these five characters.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History preface to the Confucian Scholars biography also lacks these five characters.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 尚書右丞庾持奉詔遣博士議其禮 「尚書右丞」南史作「尚書左丞」。

translations.literal: [4] "Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Chi received the edict dispatching erudites to deliberate the rites"—"right vice director" in the Southern History reads "left vice director."
translations.idiomatic: On "[4] right vice director of the masters of writing Yu Chi received the edict dispatching erudites to deliberate the rites": the Southern History reads left vice director for right vice director.

sentences.zh: 按庾持傳，持於天嘉初遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Note: in Yu Chi's biography, Chi was moved to left vice director in early Tianchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chi's biography has him moved to left vice director in early Tianchen.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 祖休稚 「休稚」南史作「休季」。

translations.literal: [5] "ancestor Xiu Zhi"—"Xiu Zhi" in the Southern History reads "Xiu Ji."
translations.idiomatic: On "[5] ancestor Xiu Zhi": the Southern History reads Xiu Ji for Xiu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 金陵局本作「休雅」，殆稚雅形近而訛。

translations.literal: The Jinling Bureau edition reads "Xiu Ya"—probably zhi and ya are graphically similar and corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinling Bureau edition reads Xiu Ya—probably zhi and ya are shape-similar corruptions.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 唯主

translations.literal: [6] "only the host"
translations.idiomatic: On "[6] only the host"

translations.literal: (sacrifice)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (sacrifice).

sentences.zh: 〔喪〕者不除 據禮記喪服小記原文改。

translations.literal: [mourning] observers do not remove—changed according to the original text of the Liji "Mourning Garments" minor record.
translations.idiomatic: On "[mourning] observers do not remove": emended per the original text of Liji, "Mourning Garments," minor record.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕 此蓋禮之正也 「正」原本訛「主」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: [7] "this is probably the correct point of ritual"—"correct" in the base text was wrong as "host"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "[7] this is probably the correct point of ritual": the base text wrongly wrote host for correct; other editions are sound; now emended.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 身無完者 「者」南、北監本及汲本並作「膚」。

translations.literal: [8] "body without intact parts"—"zhe" in the Southern and Northern Supervisory and Ji editions all read "fu" (skin).
translations.idiomatic: On "[8] body without intact parts": zhe in the Southern and Northern Supervisory and Ji editions all read fu (skin).

sentences.zh: 按漢書張耳陳餘傳正作「身無完者」，「者」作「膚」，乃後人臆改。

translations.literal: Note: the Hanshu biography of Zhang Er and Chen Yu correctly reads "body without intact parts"; writing "fu" for "zhe" is a later unwarranted emendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu biography of Zhang Er and Chen Yu correctly reads "body without intact parts"; writing fu for zhe is a later unwarranted change.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9.
translations.idiomatic: Note 9.

translations.literal: (arrive)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (arrive).

sentences.zh: 〔致〕罪人不款 據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史、元龜六一五改。

translations.literal: [bring] criminals not to kneel—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the Southern History, and Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: On "[bring] criminals not to kneel": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions, the Southern History, and Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕則〔一〕上多昔四刻 據南史及元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: [10] "then [one] on top added four quarter-mark days"—supplied according to the Southern History and Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: On "[10] then [one] on top added four quarter-mark days": supplied per the Southern History and Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 按「一上」謂行測刑一次。

translations.literal: Note: "one on top" means performing graduated punishment once.
translations.idiomatic: "One on top" means performing graduated punishment once.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕正是少日 「正」原本訛「五」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: [11] "this was few days"—"correct" in the base text was wrong as "five"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "[11] this was few days": the base text wrongly wrote five for correct; other editions are sound; now emended.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕獄囚無以在夜

translations.literal: [12] "prisoners have no means to be in the night"
translations.idiomatic: On "[12] prisoners have no means to be in the night"

translations.literal: (of)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (of).

sentences.zh: 〔而〕致誣 據各本及南史改。

translations.literal: [er] leading to false accusation—changed according to all editions and the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[er] leading to false accusation": emended per all editions and the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕羇時騁義 北監本、殿本作「羇時說朝聘義」，南史作「時羇說朝聘義」。

translations.literal: [13] "while detained he expounded meanings"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "while detained he explained court-audience meanings"; the Southern History reads "when detained he explained court-audience meanings."
translations.idiomatic: On "[13] while detained he expounded meanings": the Northern Supervisory and Hall read "while detained he explained court-audience meanings"; the Southern History reads "when detained he explained court-audience meanings."

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕太建中累遷〔鎮〕南始興王府諮議參軍 按始興王叔陵傳，叔陵於太建四年遷鎮南將軍，明「南」上脫一「鎮」字，南史有，今據補。

translations.literal: [14] "In Taijian repeatedly advanced to [Pacifies] the South Prince of Shixing's staff counsel"—according to the Shixing prince Shuling's biography, in Taijian year 4 he was made General Who Pacifies the South; clearly "south" above lacks "pacifies"; the Southern History has it; now supplied.
translations.idiomatic: On "[14] in Taijian repeatedly advanced to [pacifies] the south prince of Shixing's staff counsel": Shuling's biography has him made general who pacifies the south in Taijian year 4; south clearly lacks pacifies; the Southern History has it; now supplied.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕法雲寺沙門慧休 殿本考證云「休」南史作「拔」。

translations.literal: [15] "Fayun Temple monk Huixiu"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "xiu" in the Southern History reads "ba."
translations.idiomatic: On "[15] Fayun Temple monk Huixiu": the Hall edition notes xiu in the Southern History reads ba.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕顧越字思南 殿本考證云「思」南史作「允」。

translations.literal: [16] "Gu Yue styled Sinan"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "si" in the Southern History reads "yun."
translations.idiomatic: On "[16] Gu Yue styled Sinan": the Hall edition notes si in the Southern History reads yun.

sentences.zh: 〔一七〕傍通異義 「異」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: [17] "beside connecting variant meanings"—the character "yi" (variant) was an ink dot in the base text; supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[17] beside connecting variant meanings": the character yi (variant) was an ink dot in the base text; supplied per all editions.

sentences.zh: 〔一八〕除始興王諮議參軍 南史作「除東中郎鄱陽王府諮議參軍」。

translations.literal: [18] "appointed staff counsel to the Prince of Shixing"—the Southern History reads "appointed staff counsel to the Prince of Poyang's Eastern Center Commandant household."
translations.idiomatic: On "[18] appointed staff counsel to the prince of Shixing": the Southern History reads appointed staff counsel to the prince of Poyang's eastern center commandant household.

sentences.zh: 張森楷校勘記云：「按鄱陽王伯山傳，伯山曾為東中郎，『始興王』應依南史作『鄱陽王』。」

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "According to the Prince of Poyang Boshan's biography, Boshan once was Eastern Center Commandant—'Prince of Shixing' should follow the Southern History as 'Prince of Poyang.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai's collation note says: per Prince Poyang Boshan's biography, Boshan once was eastern center commandant—"prince of Shixing" should follow the Southern History as "prince of Poyang."

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕時年七十八 「七十八」南史作「七十七」。

translations.literal: [19] "at the time age seventy-eight"—"seventy-eight" in the Southern History reads "seventy-seven."
translations.idiomatic: On "[19] at the time age seventy-eight": seventy-eight in the Southern History reads seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕祖道寶 殿本考證云「寶」南史作「實」。

translations.literal: [20] "grandfather Dao Bao"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "bao" in the Southern History reads "shi."
translations.idiomatic: On "[20] grandfather Dao Bao": the Hall edition notes bao in the Southern History reads shi.

sentences.zh: 〔二一〕姻不失親 按語本論語「因不失其親」，此以因作婚姻解，故改「因」為「姻」。

translations.literal: [21] "marriage alliance does not lose kin"—the phrase in the Analects is "yin does not lose kin"; here yin is read as marriage alliance, so "yin" was changed to "marriage yin."
translations.idiomatic: On "[21] marriage alliance does not lose kin": the Analects reads "yin does not lose kin"; here yin is taken as marriage alliance, so yin was written as marriage yin.

sentences.zh: 詳錢大昕廿二史考異。

translations.literal: See Qian Daxin's Collation of the Twenty-Four Histories in detail.
translations.idiomatic: See Qian Daxin's Collation of the Twenty-Four Histories in detail.

sentences.zh: 〔二二〕倉卒引其母妹並孤姪入船 殿本考證云「孤」南史作「姑」。

translations.literal: [22] "hurriedly drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephew into the boat"—the Hall edition's textual verification says "orphan" in the Southern History reads "paternal aunt."
translations.idiomatic: On "[22] hurriedly drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephew into the boat": the Hall edition notes orphan in the Southern History reads paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 〔二三〕元規著春秋發題辭及義記十一卷 按：經典釋文敘錄言沈文阿撰春秋義略未竟，王元規續成之。

translations.literal: [23] "Yuangui authored Spring and Autumn Opening Topics and Expository Records eleven scrolls"—note: the Jingdian shiwen xulu says Shen Wena authored Spring and Autumn Expository Outline unfinished, and Wang Yuangui continued and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: On "[23] Yuangui authored Spring and Autumn opening topics and expository records eleven scrolls": the Jingdian shiwen xulu says Shen Wena's Spring and Autumn expository outline was unfinished and Wang Yuangui completed it.

sentences.zh: 隋書經籍志有王元規續沈文阿春秋左氏傳義略十卷。

translations.literal: The Sui Treatise on Bibliography has Wang Yuangui's Continuation of Shen Wena's Zuo Commentary Expository Outline in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise on Bibliography lists Wang Yuangui's continuation of Shen Wena's Zuo Commentary expository outline in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 此「義記」當為「義略」之訛。

translations.literal: This "Expository Records" should be the error for "Expository Outline."
translations.idiomatic: Expository Records here should be the error for Expository Outline.
